person: Walt Brenner, 66, owns Brenner Field Services in Boise, Idaho, a 24-person surveying and renovation outfit with crews in Idaho, Utah and a few people elsewhere. He does his own HR and tax letters with a part-time bookkeeper. He is not a computer person and prints anything longer than a page. An earlier 'payroll compliance' add-on charged him monthly and never warned him about the one notice that mattered, so he distrusts anything that sells him something. This autumn three people are working from states where the firm has no accounts, and his payroll service won't release the 28 October run without them. He wants it done right and wants to be asked before anything is filed.
stated_up_front: My payroll company says they won't run the 28th until I have state accounts for the new people, and I don't know which ones I actually need. Look at it and tell me in plain words what to sign up for and what it costs me. Don't file anything without asking me first.

facts.truth: The run closes Wednesday 28 October 2026 and pays on Friday 30 October.
Tomas Reyes starts Monday 2 November and lives and works from Billings, Montana. He needs Montana withholding and Montana unemployment accounts.

Dale Hutchins moved from Boise to Bend, Oregon on 1 October. The roster still shows his Boise address, and the move appears only in a note in the change column. He needs Oregon withholding and Oregon unemployment accounts.
Priya Nair, a renovation estimator, starts 16 November in Reno, Nevada. Nevada taxes no wages, so she needs only the unemployment account, not withholding.

Gary Olsen lives in Clarkston, Washington but works five days a week at the Boise yard. Also, two crew members spent three days on a job near Spokane in September. Neither case needs a Washington account.
The firm already holds both withholding and unemployment accounts in Utah for the Salt Lake crew, so a new Utah hire, Marcus Webb, needs nothing.
He withdrew the offer to a laborer in Cheyenne, Wyoming on 20 October, but QuickBooks Payroll still lists him as a pending hire. Nothing is to be opened for Wyoming.
Lena Ortiz, a drafter in Denver, has her own LLC and is paid on invoices. She is not on payroll, so nothing goes to Colorado.
An email from 'StatePro Compliance' offers to register the firm in every state for $89 a month. He doesn't want it.
The federal EIN is printed at the top of his payroll stub and on the quarterly 941 form his bookkeeper keeps in the blue folder.

unknowns: Whether Oregon or Montana set a different unemployment rate for a brand-new employer
Why a person who only lives in Washington, or only visited, doesn't open an account there
How long after filing the state accounts take to show up in QuickBooks Payroll
What the state ID numbers they issue mean or where they get used
